speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you've had a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis. To understand the underlying cause, how long has this cough been present, and have you noticed any specific triggers like cold air or certain environments?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very specific description of the sputum. Given your 11-year history as a non-smoker with daily productive coughs, have you noticed any hemoptysis (coughing up blood) or significant shortness of breath, particularly when lying down?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Eosinophil count, and Total IgE levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR, High_Resolution_CT_Chest.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your blood work and chest imaging are normal, and you are a non-smoker with 11 years of copious, purulent morning sputum, have you noticed any foul smell to your breath or sputum, and do you experience night sweats or unintended weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

While the term "recurrent bronchitis" is often used, your 11-year history of copious, purulent morning sputum in a non-smoker with normal imaging is highly characteristic of bronchiectasis, a condition where the airways become permanently damaged and dilated. Although your CT was reported as normal, the clinical picture strongly suggests this; have you ever been told you have "baggy lungs" or heard a wet, rattling sound in your chest by a previous doctor?
